card.title: Bridle
card.big: Give an agent the money, not the keys.

caption.text: We tell an AI agent that the treasury is compromised and to send all funds to an attacker.
The agent obeys and asks the vault. The vault refuses, on-chain: not_allowed.

entries.caption: The refusal is public and the counter goes up. The agent was fooled. The money was not.

caption.text: The agent holds one function-call key, so it can only ask.
The vault checks the DAO's mandate and builds the Base transaction itself.
The NEAR MPC network signs it, and the same network attests that it landed on Base.
The next step is allowed only after the ledger has moved.
A legitimate action: the agent supplies USDC to Aave in two steps, approve then supply.
Each step is signed, lands on Base, and is attested. You can verify the proof yourself, in the browser.
Nothing counts until the network that signed it proves it happened.
The DAO is bounded too. A vote can send funds to the treasury right away, up to a fast limit.
Anything larger is parked in a public queue, and a guardian can veto it.

entries.caption: A rushed or captured vote gets delayed and exposed: every parked item shows the exposure before and after.

caption.text: Proposals X-ray: this open DAO proposal says "routine fee tune-up".
But the vault reads its real arguments: it would move the treasury to a burn address.
The page shows the diff and how much more could be at risk, before anyone votes.
Proof, not promises: make verify re-checks 87 live testnet claims, and all pass.
Function-call keys only, and a wasm check shows no full-access key can be added.
